limits: One sequential socket/shared pair per desktop, without randomized order or repeated independent runs.

Arch is Xvfb/Core Graphics at 960x540 with default VNC timing; SteamOS is accelerated Xorg/Metal presentation at 1560x1112 with adaptive timing. Compare modes within a desktop; these are not matched cross-distribution workloads.
Controlled fullscreen Xlib color/strip repaints do not establish real desktop/game FPS, sustained performance, battery life or physical input-to-panel latency.
SteamOS shared run began nominal and ended at fair thermal state; matched-thermal repeats remain unqualified. This observation does not establish that shared capture caused heating.
The known x11vnc SIGKILL SysV resource-lifetime issue remains. These measurements do not qualify crash cleanup or promote shared capture to default.
Earlier instrumentation pilots are excluded. Final runs use larger encoded markers and receiver timestamps retained under the frame lock, associated synchronously with the submitted snapshot.

Native instrumentation adds observer overhead. Missing generated IDs can be coalesced before decode or at native submission. Arch/shared decoded 56 distinct burst IDs and submitted 55; every other run submitted all decoded IDs.
